input: For a DBS HDB loan, what's the max LTV and min cash downpayment if the flat's valuation is below the purchase price?

input: What is the TDSR cap for DBS home loans, and what is the MSR cap and does it apply to HDB flats?
expected_output: The TDSR is capped at 55% of all borrowers' gross monthly income. The MSR is capped at 30% of all borrowers' gross monthly income and applies only to HDB flat purchases.
context:
DBS Mortgage Calculator (DBS) — https://www.dbs.com.sg/personal/landing/loans/homeloans/calculate-loans.html
Income and Financial Commitment
In calculating your maximum home loan amount, banks will take into account the ratio of your debt to your income. This is called the Total Debt Servicing Ratio (TDSR) and this ratio is capped at 55% of all borrowers' gross monthly income.
If you are purchasing a HDB flat, banks also have to calculate your Mortgage Servicing Ratio (MSR). MSR is capped at 30% of all borrowers' gross monthly income. Calculation of MSR is based on loan amount and combined monthly gross income.
Your maximum home loan amount is determined by TDSR, MSR (for HDB only), loan tenure and a medium-term 3.5% interest rate.
Check out our calculators below to find out how much you can borrow.

input: Does DBS use the Rule of 78 for personal loan interest, and how does it affect my early repayment?
expected_output: Yes. DBS uses the Rule of 78 (sum of digits) method to apportion interest in its personal loan instalments. Earlier months allocate a larger share of each instalment to interest, and this share declines over time. For example, on a S$3,000 loan at 1.99% p.a. over 12 months, month 1's S$254.97 instalment is S$9.18 interest and S$245.79 principal.
context:
DBS Personal Loan (DBS) — https://www.dbs.com.sg/personal/loans/instant-cash/personal-loan
Assuming that you are taking a loan of S$3,000 at 1.99% p.a. + 1% processing fee for 12 months (EIR 5.47% p.a.2):
Principal loan amount: S$3,000
Interest payable for 12 months tenure: S$59.70
One-time processing fee: S$30 (Billed together with the first month instalment)
Estimated monthly instalment amount: S$254.97
Interest amortisation:
The amortisation of the amount of interest payment allocated to the monthly instalment is calculated using the Rule of 78 method (which is also known as the sum of digits method). Monthly interest and principal are apportioned differently; in the earlier months, a larger portion of your monthly repayment goes towards paying off the interest on the loan and gradually decreases over time. input: If I miss the minimum payment due date on my DBS Cashline, does the interest rate go up by 8% p.a., and does paying in July remove it?
expected_output: Yes. If the minimum payment isn't received by the due date (e.g., 25 Jun), the interest rate rises by 8% p.a. on top of the Prevailing Interest Rate. No, paying in July does not remove it: the increase still applies even if the minimum payment is received on or before the following month's due date.
context:
DBS Cashline (DBS) — https://www.dbs.com.sg/personal/loans/instant-cash/cashline
Alternatively, you may also make repayment via AXS or DBS/POSB ATMs.
If the Bank does not receive the required minimum payment by its due date (for example, due date on 25 Jun as illustrated in the example below), the interest rate applicable to your DBS/POSB Cashline account will be increased by 8% p.a. on top of the Prevailing Interest Rate (“Increased Interest Rate”). This Increased Interest Rate shall be applied to the outstanding balance in your DBS/POSB Cashline account from the first working day after the date of the subsequent DBS/POSB Cashline account statement following your DBS/POSB Cashline account statement (i.e. August’s statement) and used to compute the finance charges applicable to your DBS/POSB Cashline account.
This additional interest rate shall be applied even if minimum payment is received by the Bank on or before the due date of the following month (i.e. in July).
